# Unity

## Detect
- Editor version: `m_EditorVersion` in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`. Build and test only with that exact Editor; another version reimports and upgrades the project.
- Render pipeline: `com.unity.render-pipelines.universal` (URP) or `com.unity.render-pipelines.high-definition` (HDRP) in `Packages/manifest.json`, plus the active Render Pipeline Asset: the one a Quality level assigns, else the default in Graphics settings; no asset means Built-in, which Unity 6.5 deprecates (supported through the 6.7 LTS; as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.5 upgrade guide). Shaders and materials do not port between pipelines.
- Packages: `Packages/manifest.json` (requested) and `Packages/packages-lock.json` (resolved); embedded packages live in `Packages/<name>/`.
- Packages outside `Assets/` and `Packages/` (for example at the repository root): their C# files are not matched by the default globs. Bind the package folder to both `unity` and `unity-upm` with `stack_paths` in the profile, keeping each pack's default globs the project still needs in its list (for example a host project's `**/Assets/**/*.cs`; see `[stack_paths]` in the [profile template](.ai/kit/core/templates/project/profile.toml)), and activate both.
- Assemblies: `.asmdef`/`.asmref` files. Scripts outside any asmdef compile into `Assembly-CSharp`, or `Assembly-CSharp-Editor` when under an `Editor` folder; under the top-level `Assets/Plugins` folder they compile first, into `Assembly-CSharp-firstpass` or `Assembly-CSharp-Editor-firstpass`.
- Player settings in `ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset`: scripting backend (Mono or IL2CPP), API compatibility level, active input handling (Input Manager, Input System package, or both).
- Asset serialization mode must be Force Text (Project Settings > Editor) for scene, prefab, and asset diffs to be readable.
- Editor availability, before changing serialized assets: an Editor has the project open, an installed Editor can run batch mode, or neither. It selects the route in «Conventions». An open Editor that does not answer is not "neither": compile errors start it in Safe Mode, where no bridge package loads, so fix the C# errors; a sandboxed shell can hide a running Editor, so ask the user whether one is open; a modal dialog can block it, so report the dialog. Rule these out before taking route 2 or 3.
- `com.unity.pipeline` in `Packages/manifest.json`: the project uses the Unity CLI as its live-Editor bridge (route 1); read the Editor's state with `unity status` and results by the exit codes in «Version Notes».

## Conventions
- Keep `UnityEditor` code out of player builds: put it in an `Editor` folder or an asmdef whose `includePlatforms` is `["Editor"]`; guard Editor calls in runtime scripts with `#if UNITY_EDITOR`. A runtime assembly that references `UnityEditor` fails the player build.
- Declare a new asmdef's references explicitly; asmdefs cannot reference the predefined `Assembly-CSharp*` assemblies, and references must not form cycles.
- Commit every `.meta` file and move or rename it with its asset (prefer the Editor or `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset`). The `.meta` holds the GUID that all references use; deleting or regenerating it breaks references silently.
- Name each `MonoBehaviour`/`ScriptableObject` file exactly after its class.
- Expose inspector fields with `[SerializeField] private`, not public fields. When renaming a serialized field, add `[FormerlySerializedAs("oldName")]` (`UnityEngine.Serialization`); without it the stored value is dropped.
- Change scenes, prefabs, and other serialized assets by the first route that applies. Unity advises against editing its YAML directly: `fileID`/GUID links and prefab overrides break silently.
  1. A live Editor is reachable (a live-Editor bridge the project already uses, or a user who runs your menu item): change the asset through it with an Editor script or menu item (`SerializedObject`, `PrefabUtility.LoadPrefabContents` → `SaveAsPrefabAsset` → `UnloadPrefabContents`, `EditorSceneManager`, `AssetDatabase`). Never hand-edit then: the running Editor misses the change until reimport.
  2. No Editor has the project open and one is installed: run a static Editor method with `<Unity> -batchmode -quit -projectPath <path> -executeMethod <Class.Method> -logFile <file>`; the method saves its changes and throws or calls `EditorApplication.Exit(1)` on failure. For asynchronous work (for example Package Manager `Client` requests), omit `-quit`, which can hang on asynchronous code, and call `EditorApplication.Exit` once the work completes. A batch run cannot observe its result (a reference saved as null still reports success), so confirm it in the log, an EditMode test, or the next Editor load.
  3. Neither is possible: direct YAML editing is a declared exception. Edit only text files (Force Text; first line `%YAML 1.1`), copy the shape of an existing block of the same class, and give each new object an `&<id>` anchor unused in the file. Never touch `PrefabInstance` documents, `m_Modifications`, or `stripped` objects; stop and report instead. State "edited Unity YAML directly; no Editor available" in the report.
  4. After any direct YAML edit, verify before finishing: each `--- !u!<class> &<id>` anchor is unique in the file; each non-zero local `{fileID: N}` matches an anchor in the file; each `guid` in the edited blocks matches a `.meta` in the project or a package; `m_Father` ↔ `m_Children` and `m_GameObject` ↔ `m_Component` agree both ways. At the next opportunity, load the file in the Editor or batch mode and read the console or log for malformed-YAML errors.
- Lifecycle: `Awake` → `OnEnable` → `Start` → `FixedUpdate` → `Update` → `LateUpdate`; teardown `OnDisable` → `OnDestroy`. Initialize self in `Awake`, reach other objects in `Start`; order across objects is undefined unless set with `[DefaultExecutionOrder]` or Script Execution Order.
- Physics in `FixedUpdate`, camera follow in `LateUpdate`; scale per-frame motion by `Time.deltaTime`.
- In `Update`, `FixedUpdate`, and `LateUpdate`: use references cached in `Awake`/`Start`; never call `GetComponent`, `FindObjectsByType`, or `GameObject.Find`; avoid allocations (LINQ, closures, string concatenation, new collections, boxing); use `CompareTag` and non-allocating physics queries.
- Call Unity APIs only from the main thread.

## Verify
- Prefer `commands.build` and `commands.test`.
- Compile check: `<Unity> -batchmode -quit -projectPath <path> -logFile <file>`; a non-zero exit code or `error CS` in the log is a failure. Batch mode cannot open a project that an Editor already has open.
- Tests (Unity Test Framework): `<Unity> -batchmode -projectPath <path> -runTests -testPlatform EditMode|PlayMode -testResults <file.xml> -logFile <file>`; narrow with `-testFilter` or `-testCategory`. Omit `-quit`; it is not supported while tests run, and the runner exits when done.
- A raw `-runTests` run has no common exit-code definition: the results XML is the verdict, and a run that wrote no XML has no verdict, never a pass. Through the Unity CLI, read its exit codes instead (see «Version Notes»).
- After changing anything through an Editor, its console shows no errors. Entering Play Mode proves nothing until frames advance: an unfocused Editor can stay on frame 1 while it reports Play Mode.
- Test asmdefs reference the test runner assemblies; EditMode test asmdefs include only the `Editor` platform.

## Pitfalls
- `UnityEngine.Object` overrides `==`: a destroyed object equals `null`, but `?.`, `??`, and `is null` bypass that check. Use `== null` or the implicit bool for Unity objects.
- Constructors on `MonoBehaviour` may run outside Play Mode and off the main thread; initialize in `Awake`. Create components with `AddComponent` and scriptable objects with `ScriptableObject.CreateInstance`, never `new`.
- Changing a field's default in code does not update instances already serialized in scenes and prefabs; they keep their stored values.
- IL2CPP code stripping removes members reached only through reflection; keep them with `[Preserve]` or `link.xml`.
- Editing `Library/`, `Temp/`, `Logs/`, or `obj/`: they are generated caches and are not committed.
- Assuming a fresh git worktree is ready: it has no `Library/`. Each worktree is its own project folder with its own `Library/`; never share, link, or commit it. The first Editor or batch run there performs a full import that costs time and disk, unless the worktree was seeded (see «Version Notes»). Untracked links or junctions (for example ones exposing `Samples~` to a host project) are missing too; recreate them or work in the checkout that has them.
- Mixing mass reserialization (`AssetDatabase.ForceReserializeAssets`) into a feature change: it rewrites many files and buries the real diff. Run it only when requested, as its own change. Unity 6.6 always turns off YAML word wrapping and removes the Reduce Version Control Noise option that used to control it, so a project that had the option off sees wrapped lines change as files are saved; keep those diffs out of feature changes too (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.6 upgrade guide).
- Changing a `ScriptableObject` asset in Play Mode in the Editor persists after exiting Play Mode; copy it with `Instantiate` for runtime state.

## Version Notes
- Unity 6 Editor versions are numbered `6000.x`: 6.0 LTS (supported through October 2026), 6.3 LTS (until December 2027), 6.6 as the supported Update release, and 6.7 in beta as the next LTS; Unity 7 (`7000.x`) is in alpha (as of 2026-10-28, per unity.com/releases, the Unity 6 support page, and the Unity release API).
- Unity 6.3 allows `[SerializeField]` only on fields: on a property, method, or type it is a compile error; serialize an auto-property through its backing field with `[field: SerializeField]` (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.3 upgrade guide).
- Unity 6.5 replaces `InstanceID` with `EntityId`: the obsolete `InstanceID` APIs are compile errors whose messages usually name the replacement (`GetInstanceID()` → `GetEntityId()`). An `EntityId` is 8 bytes, so never store it in an `int` or key data by its `GetHashCode()`. 6.5 also removes the obsolete `GameObject`/`Component` shortcut properties (`rigidbody`, `renderer`, `collider`, and others) and `AddComponent(string)` (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.5 upgrade guide).
- Unity 6.5 drops project and package copies of `System.Text.Json` and three other class-library assemblies it now provides, and 6.6 deprecates the `UNITY_64` and `DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` defines. Both affect project code too; the [`unity-upm`](.ai/kit/core/stacks/frameworks/unity-upm.md) pack's «Version Notes» list the assemblies and the replacement defines (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.5 and 6.6 upgrade guides).
- Unity 6.6 serializes `[SerializeField] Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` fields; types that derive from or wrap a dictionary keep their own serialization. Migrating a field moves no data: add the new field beside the old one, copy the data with an Editor script, verify it, and only then delete the old field (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.6 upgrade guide).
- New Unity 6.6 projects enter Play Mode with Reload Scene only (no domain reload), so static fields and static event handlers keep their values from the previous Play session; read Enter Play Mode Settings (Project Settings > Editor) before relying on either behavior. From 6.5, `[AutoStaticsCleanup]` (`Unity.Scripting.LifecycleManagement`, on a `partial` type) resets the statics it marks when Play Mode starts (as of 2026-10, per What's New in Unity 6.6 and the Unity 6000.5 Scripting API).
- From Unity 6.5 the Editor writes its log to `<Project>/Logs/Editor.log` by default instead of one per-user file; code reads the path from `Application.consoleLogPath` (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.5 upgrade guide).
- `Awaitable` (async/await support) exists from Unity 2023.1 and Unity 6; check the project's version before replacing coroutines (as of 2026-10, per Unity Scripting API).
- `Object.FindObjectOfType`/`FindObjectsOfType` are obsolete in Unity 6; use `FindFirstObjectByType`, `FindAnyObjectByType`, or `FindObjectsByType`. From Unity 6.4, `FindObjectsSortMode` and the overloads taking it are obsolete too; call the overloads without it (as of 2026-10, per Unity Scripting API).
- URP custom render passes differ when Render Graph is enabled (the default for new URP projects in Unity 6). Unity 6.3 removes URP Compatibility Mode (its `URP_COMPATIBILITY_MODE` define only helps convert a project, and Unity 6.4 removes the define), so custom passes on 6.3 and later must use the Render Graph API; on 6.0–6.2 check the Compatibility Mode setting before writing `ScriptableRenderPass` code (as of 2026-10, per the Unity 6.3 and 6.4 upgrade guides).
- From Unity 6.2, Unity logs explicit errors for some malformed `.unity`, `.prefab`, and `.asset` files: unknown types, scripts on types that cannot host them, `!u!` header and type mismatches, missing headers, and general parse errors such as an invalid type ID or a malformed header. The checks are not exhaustive; earlier versions often discard malformed data without reporting it (as of 2026-10, per Unity's technical article on Unity Discussions, 2025-09-19).
- Example live-Editor bridge, never a requirement: the Unity CLI (`unity`, 1.0.0-beta.14 on 2026-10-21; no stable release yet) drives a running Unity 6.0+ Editor through the `com.unity.pipeline` package (`unity status`, `unity command`). Its `unity mcp` replaces the deprecated MCP server of the in-Editor AI assistant package; from a shell, `unity command` drives the Editor directly, faster and with fewer tokens than MCP (as of 2026-10, per docs.unity.com Unity CLI release notes and "Replace MCP server with Unity CLI").
- Unity CLI exit codes: `unity test` returns 0 when every test passed, 8 when tests ran and some failed (never rerun for a pass), and 6 when the run did not finish (compile error, license, crash, or `--timeout`), which is no verdict. `unity recompile` returns 7 when it cannot reach a running Editor, so compilation is unknown, not failed; an Editor that started in Safe Mode also returns 7, and `unity status` lists its compile errors. On a Unity 6000.7 or later Editor, `unity status` names a blocking modal dialog with `STATUS_BLOCKED_BY_DIALOG`; earlier Editors read only `starting` (`STATUS_NOT_READY`), or `unreachable` once nothing has queried them for 60 seconds, so a long `starting` can be a dialog. An Editor waiting at the "Enter Safe Mode?" prompt reports `STATUS_BLOCKED_BY_DIALOG_SAFE_MODE`, quoting its first compile errors when it can read the Editor log. `unity test` refuses a project an Editor has open: run the tests in that Editor, outside Play Mode, instead of closing it (as of 2026-10, CLI 1.0.0-beta.14, per the Unity CLI reference and release notes and the official `unity-cli` agent skill).
- `unity vcs git worktree add <branch> --into <path> --seed cache|full|none` creates a worktree with a seeded `Library/`; the default seed leaves out `PackageCache/`, which the Package Manager refills during import. Run one Editor per worktree, and when several Editors run, pass `--project-path` to every call that reaches one; `recompile` and `close` ignore `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` (as of 2026-10, per the official `unity-cli` agent skill and its version-control reference).
